column3: “leprosy” renders “tsara’at,” a serious skin disease, not necessarily modern leprosy (throughout the chapter); “an infection” renders “nega’ (a plague, stroke),” and “a scab” renders “a flaking (sappahat).”
“has faded” renders “has become dull,” and “a scab” renders “a rash (mispahat)” (also in verses 7–8).
“spreads farther” renders an emphatic doubled verb (also in verses 22, 27 and 35).
“quick raw flesh” renders “a raw spot of living flesh.”
“breaks out farther” renders an emphatic doubled verb, and “as far as the priest can see” renders “to all the sight of the eyes of the priest.”
